newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips close shade higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips close shade higher.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks closed modestly higher in slack turnover Friday but the underlying trend remained weak, dealers said.

"Stocks responded calmly to economic indicators today, which weren't great but quelled the storm in the markets," said Banco Santander's chief researcher Dario Lizzano referring to U.S. inflation data.
He predicted stocks would switch back to losses and remain thinly traded early next week.
The blue-chip MerVal index firmed 0.4 percent to 711.7, trimming the week's losses to 2.6 percent.
The MerVal stands 0.8 percent lower so far in March after rising steadily in recent months.

"Nobody knows whether the trend has changed or not," another trader said. "We'll only know if it's a bearish period or just a downwards correction after the U.S. Federal Reserve meets March 25 and the markets are able to carry on with business without the constant threat of a rate hike."
Floor turnover dwindled to 16.9 million pesos from an already weakened volume of 26 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals eased to 104.9 million pesos from 127.9 million Thursday.
The broad market index closed off 0.1 percent, with winners outpacing losers 26 to 17 and 19 issues closing flat.
Strongest main-tier performers were footwear and textile firm Alpargatas, steelmaker Acindar and construction stock Polledo, which jumped 3.4 percent, 2.7 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively.

The MerVal's heaviest loss of 2.5 percent was posted by oil company Astra, which was downgraded from buy to hold Thursday by Fleming. Steelmaker Siderar shed 1.7 percent and petrochemical concern Indupa closed off 0.8 percent.
